def-ql-quasi.title: Quasi-likelihood
def-ql-quasi.html:
Under @def-ql-variance-function, the quasi-likelihood of a mean μ∈M given a response y in the closure of M, with weight w, is Q(μ;y)=wϕ∫yμy−tV(t)dt,{#eq-ql-quasi}

assumed finite, the integral being read as a limit at an endpoint of M where it converges — as it does at y=0 for V(t)=t and at y∈{0,1} for V(t)=t(1−t). The quasi-likelihood of the model is 𝛃Q(β)=∑i=1nQ(μi;yi) with 𝛃μi=h(x(i)⊤β) and weight wi.

def-ql-variance-function.title: A variance specification
def-ql-variance-function.html:
Let Y1,…,Yn be independent, let w1,…,wn>0 be known weights, let g be a strictly monotone differentiable link with inverse h, and let V be a positive, continuously differentiable function on an open interval M⊆R. A variance specification is the pair of assumptions 𝛃E(Yi)=μi=h(x(i)⊤β),Var(Yi)=ϕV(μi)wi,{#eq-ql-specification}

with 𝛃β∈Rp and ϕ>0 unknown. The function V is the variance function and ϕ the dispersion. No distribution is assumed for Yi beyond these two moments.

eq-ql-contagion.html: VarYEY=ES2ES ≥ ES ≥ 1,

eq-ql-equations.html: ∑i=1nxijwih′(ηi)V(μi)(yi−μi)=0,j=1,…,p,

eq-ql-exchangeable.html: E(Z¯)=π,Var(Z¯)={1+ρ(m−1)}π(1−π)m,

eq-ql-meat.html: 𝛃Cov{U(β0)}=Bn=1ϕ2∑i=1n{wih′(ηi)V(μi)}2σi2x(i)x(i)⊤,

eq-ql-quasi.html: Q(μ;y)=wϕ∫yμy−tV(t)dt,

eq-ql-quasi-deviance.html: 𝛍𝛃D(y,μ)=−2ϕQ(β)=2∑i=1nwi∫μiyiyi−tV(t)dt ≥0,

eq-ql-quasi-f.html: 𝛍𝛍F={D(y,μ~)−D(y,μ^)}/qϕ^P.

eq-ql-robust.html: Σ^rob=(X⊤W^X)−1{∑i=1nc^i2(yi−μ^i)2x(i)x(i)⊤}(X⊤W^X)−1,

eq-ql-sandwich-limit.html: 𝛃𝛃Bn−1/2An(β^−β0) →d Np(0,I),

eq-ql-size.html: Pr{χ2(q)>χ1−α2(q)/ϕ0} ≥ α,

eq-ql-specification.html: 𝛃E(Yi)=μi=h(x(i)⊤β),Var(Yi)=ϕV(μi)wi,

exm-ql-coverage.title: Coverage when the variance function is right and when it is wrong
exm-ql-coverage.title_html: Coverage when the variance function is right and when it is wrong
exm-ql-coverage.html:
A quasi-Poisson model log⁡μi=β0+β1xi was fitted to data simulated with the same mean and two true variances, Var(Yi)=μi+2μi2 (quadratic) and Var(Yi)=9μi (linear), over 3000 replicates at each of seven sample sizes. Figure 38.3.1 records the coverage of nominal 95% intervals for β1 from four standard errors: Poisson with ϕ=1, model-based scaled by ϕ^, the empirical sandwich @eq-ql-robust, and a leverage-corrected sandwich described below.

Ignoring the dispersion is fatal in both panels and does not improve with n: 0.334 at n=20 and 0.323 at n=1280 in the quadratic case, 0.513 and 0.482 in the linear case. A linear true variance makes the specification correct and the ϕ^-scaled interval already good at n=20, covering 0.919 against the sandwich’s 0.880; a quadratic one stops it improving, at 0.914 for n=1280, while the sandwich climbs to 0.941, buying correctness in the limit at the price of noise in small samples, as in @exm-het-hc-coverage.

exm-ql-size.title: A test that rejects six times too often
exm-ql-size.title_html: A test that rejects six times too often
exm-ql-size.html: Counts were simulated with a constant mean 6.0, a variance 4.0 times the mean and a true slope of zero, and a Poisson log-linear model was fitted to each of 5000 data sets of size 100. Referring the drop in deviance to χ2(1) rejects at the nominal 5% level in 0.322 of the replicates — @eq-ql-size predicts 0.327 at ϕ0=4 — with the statistic averaging 3.90 against a χ2(1) mean of one. Dividing by ϕ^P and referring to F(1,98) rejects in 0.051, and the sandwich Wald test @eq-ql-robust in 0.058 (Figure 38.4.1).

exm-ql-strikes-choice.title: Four analyses of the strike data
exm-ql-strikes-choice.title_html: Four analyses of the strike data
exm-ql-strikes-choice.html:
Continuing @exm-ql-strikes-fit and @exm-ql-strikes-errors, the production coefficient under four treatments of the extra variability is

fit coefficient standard error
Poisson, ϕ=1 −7.680 0.406
quasi-Poisson, V=ϕμ −7.680 2.564
NB1, Var=ϕμ −4.934 1.983
NB2, Var=μ+μ2/κ −9.327 2.931

The NB1 fit has ϕ^=42.78, close to the quasi-Poisson ϕ^P=39.89, and the same variance function; yet its coefficient differs by more than a standard error, because its estimating equation @eq-cnt-nb1-score is not @eq-ql-equations — the warning of Section 38.1 in numbers. The NB2 fit, with α^=1/κ^=0.954, gives −9.327 against the −9.353 of the quasi model with V(μ)=μ2: at these fitted means the quadratic term of the NB2 variance dominates, so the two nearly coincide.

The tests agree on the conclusion and not on its strength. The drop in deviance is 350.9, overwhelming as χ2(1); the quasi-F statistic @eq-ql-quasi-f is 8.80 on (1,60) degrees of freedom, p=0.0043, and the score test for overdispersion @eq-cnt-score-test is 224.5. Unanticipated production predicts shorter strikes, at about the evidence a t statistic of three provides; the Poisson analysis overstates that by orders of magnitude.

exm-ql-strikes-errors.title: Four standard errors for the strike data
exm-ql-strikes-errors.title_html: Four standard errors for the strike data
exm-ql-strikes-errors.html:
Continue @exm-ql-strikes-fit. The Pearson statistic is 2393.5 on 60 degrees of freedom, so ϕ^P=39.89, against ϕ^D=37.22 from the quasi-deviance. The four standard errors for the production coefficient −7.680 are

covariance standard error t
Poisson, ϕ=1 0.406 −18.92
model-based, ϕ^P 2.564 −3.00
empirical sandwich 2.573 −2.98
leverage-corrected sandwich 2.896 −2.65

The Poisson standard error is too small by a factor of about six. More interesting are the second and third rows: the sandwich exceeds the model-based value by a factor of only 1.004, which is evidence for the quasi-Poisson variance function, so the model-based standard error is valid and slightly more efficient. The fourth row divides each squared residual by (1−hii)2, with hii the leverages of the weighted hat matrix of @def-glm-residuals; the largest is 0.192, enough to matter at n=62.

exm-ql-strikes-fit.title: Strike durations
exm-ql-strikes-fit.html:
Kennan’s data record the length in days of 62 strikes in US manufacturing, with a measure of unanticipated industrial production at the time each strike began. Take a log link and V(μ)=μ. The production coefficient is −7.680; replacing V(μ)=μ by V(μ)=7.5μ returns the same number to ten decimal places, since ϕ cancels from @eq-ql-equations, while V(μ)=μ2 moves it to −9.353, a quadratic variance function downweighting the long strikes.

The mean duration is 42.66 days and the sample variance 2102.7, nearly fifty times as large: a Poisson likelihood is no serious description of these data, and the question is how much of the Poisson machinery survives anyway.

exr-ql-beta-binomial.title: B1
exr-ql-beta-binomial.html: Let Π have a beta distribution with parameters a,b>0, so that EΠ=μ=a/(a+b) and VarΠ=μ(1−μ)/(a+b+1), and let mY¯ be binomial (m,Π) given Π. Show that EY¯=μ and Var(Y¯)={1+ρ(m−1)}μ(1−μ)m,ρ=1a+b+1, so the beta-binomial has the variance function of @eq-ql-exchangeable. Deduce that the beta-binomial and an exchangeable-trials model with the same ρ cannot be told apart by first and second moments.

exr-ql-binomial-detect.title: B2
exr-ql-binomial-detect.html: Grouped binomial data have group sizes mi spread between 2 and 50. Show that under the constant-dispersion specification the Pearson terms mi(yi−μ^i)2/{μ^i(1−μ^i)} have expectation ϕ free of mi, while under @eq-ql-exchangeable they have expectation 1+ρ(mi−1). Describe the plot this suggests and what each specification predicts for it.

exr-ql-compound-numbers.title: B1
exr-ql-compound-numbers.html: In @prp-ql-overdispersion(c), let S be geometric on {1,2,…} with mean 1/θ. Compute VarY/EY and show that it equals (2−θ)/θ. For which θ does the compound Poisson have the variance-to-mean ratio of a negative binomial with κ=μ?

exr-ql-crossing.title: A2
exr-ql-crossing.html: Two analysts fit grouped binomial data with group sizes between 5 and 60, one using a constant dispersion ϕ and one using the exchangeable form @eq-ql-exchangeable with correlation ρ. They report ϕ^=2.5 and ρ^=0.04. At which group size do the two fitted variances agree? For which groups does the first analyst’s model claim the larger variance?

exr-ql-efficiency-loss.title: B2
exr-ql-efficiency-loss.html: Let Var(Yi)=σi2 and consider the quasi-score built from a working variance function V. Using @prp-ql-optimality with the true variances, show that An−1BnAn−1 — the asymptotic covariance of @thm-ql-asymptotics(a) — is never smaller, in the nonnegative definite order, than the inverse Godambe information (∑ih′(ηi)2σi−2x(i)x(i)⊤)−1 of the best linear estimating function, and that the two agree exactly when σi2∝V(μi)/wi.

exr-ql-hand-optimality.title: B1
exr-ql-hand-optimality.html: Take n independent responses with EYi=μ (one unknown parameter, no regressors) and VarYi=ϕV(μ)/wi. Show that the quasi-score estimate of @thm-ql-score is the weighted mean ∑iwiyi/∑iwi, and verify @prp-ql-optimality directly: among estimating functions ∑iai(yi−μ) with constants ai, the Godambe information is maximized by ai∝wi.

exr-ql-information-test.title: C1
exr-ql-information-test.html: A large discrepancy between ϕ^P(X⊤W^X)−1 and @eq-ql-robust is evidence that the variance specification is wrong. Propose a test statistic from the difference of the two matrices, say tr{(X⊤W^X)Σ^rob}−pϕ^P, argue informally that its mean is about zero when the specification is correct, and say what stands in the way of a usable null distribution. (This is White’s information matrix test; compare @exr-het-white-test.)

exr-ql-integrability.title: C1
exr-ql-integrability.html: Take the quasi-binomial specification V(t)=t(1−t) on (0,1) with w=1 and any ϕ>0. (a) Show that y↦exp⁡{Q(μ;y)} is integrable over (0,1), so normalizes to a density f. (b) Show that a distribution on [0,1] with mean m has variance at most m(1−m), with equality only on {0,1}; deduce that f has variance strictly below m(1−m) at its own mean m, never ϕm(1−m) with ϕ≥1. (c) Show that f is symmetric about 1/2 when μ=1/2, and check numerically that at μ=0.3, ϕ=1 it has mean 0.4408 and variance 0.0687, against μ=0.3 and ϕμ(1−μ)=0.21. Conclude that integrability of exp⁡Q does not make a variance specification a family.

exr-ql-intercept-sandwich.title: B1
exr-ql-intercept-sandwich.html: Take an intercept-only quasi-Poisson model, log⁡μi=β for all i. Show that μ^i=y¯, that the model-based variance of β^ is ϕ^P/(ny¯), and that the sandwich variance is ∑i(yi−y¯)2/(ny¯)2. Show that the two agree exactly when ϕ^P is computed with divisor n rather than n−p.

exr-ql-lognormal-shape.title: C1
exr-ql-lognormal-shape.html:
@prp-ql-overdispersion(a) says that unmodelled heterogeneity overdisperses. It says nothing about the shape of the excess, and the shape decides the repair. Suppose that, given an unrecorded Zi∼N(0,1) independent of the covariate, Yi is Poisson with mean Λi=exp⁡(β0+β1xi+γZi), γ≠0.

  1. Using @thm-mvn-mgf, show that μi=E(Yi)=exp⁡(β0+γ2/2+β1xi): the marginal mean is still log-linear, with the same slope and a raised intercept. So the mean model is not at fault, and this is not case (d) of the proposition.

  2. Show that Var(Yi)=μi+(eγ2−1)μi2, so that Var(Yi)E(Yi)=1+(eγ2−1)μi, which increases with the mean instead of being constant.

  3. Which of the four devices in the table of this section is the right one, and what does the plot of squared Pearson residuals against μ^i look like under the true model and under the quasi-Poisson specification V(μ)=ϕμ?

  4. Show that β^1 from the quasi-Poisson fit is still consistent, and explain why no single ϕ^ makes the reported standard errors right across a design whose fitted means vary widely.

exr-ql-marginals.title: B2
exr-ql-marginals.html: Suppose the link satisfies g′(μ)=1/V(μ), the canonical link of the variance function. Show that @eq-ql-equations becomes ∑iwixij(yi−μ^i)=0 for every j, so that the fit reproduces the weighted column totals of X exactly, as in @cor-glm-marginals. Check the condition for V(μ)=μ with a log link and for V(μ)=μ(1−μ) with a logit link, and find the canonical link of V(μ)=μ2.

exr-ql-mean-model-first.title: A2
exr-ql-mean-model-first.html: A Poisson regression of accident counts on three covariates gives X2/(n−p)=3.2. Give three distinct explanations, and for each one say what you would compute next.

exr-ql-mixture-bound.title: C1
exr-ql-mixture-bound.html: Let Y∣Λ have mean Λ and variance aΛξ, and let Λ have mean μ and finite variance τ2. Show that the marginal variance is aE(Λξ)+τ2, equal to aμ+τ2 when ξ=1. For ξ=2, use Jensen’s inequality to show that it is at least aμ2+τ2, so a mixture of quasi-gamma responses is overdispersed relative to the quasi-gamma specification with the same a.

exr-ql-nb-quasi.title: A2
exr-ql-nb-quasi.html: Show that the NB2 variance function V(μ)=μ+μ2/κ with κ known gives ϕw−1Q(μ;y)=ylog⁡{μ/(μ+κ)}+κlog⁡{κ/(μ+κ)} up to a function of y, which is the negative binomial log-likelihood kernel of @eq-cnt-nb-pmf. NB2 with κ known is an exponential dispersion family, so @prp-ql-properties(c) applies; explain why the quasi-Poisson specification V(μ)=μ with ϕ free does not enjoy the same conclusion, and relate this to the remark of Section 38.1.

exr-ql-nb1-vs-quasi.title: B3
exr-ql-nb1-vs-quasi.html: Both the NB1 model and the quasi-Poisson specification have Var(Yi)=ϕμi. Using @eq-cnt-nb1-score and @eq-ql-equations, explain why a single very large count influences the two fits differently, and predict which of the two coefficients in @exm-ql-strikes-choice would move more if the longest strike were deleted.

exr-ql-no-scalar-dispersion.title: C2
exr-ql-no-scalar-dispersion.html:
@prp-ql-overdispersion(b) attributes the inflation 1+ρ(m−1) to clustering. When the individual units, and not their averages, are the data, a scalar dispersion parameter cannot represent it at all. Let the data be Yij, j=1,…,ni, i=1,…,m, with means μij, marginal variance σ2 throughout, exchangeable within-cluster correlation ρ∈(0,1) (@eq-ql-exchangeable) and independence across clusters, and let S=∑ijaijYij for constants aij.

  1. Show that Var(S)=σ2∑i{(1−ρ)∑jaij2+ρ(∑jaij)2}.

  2. Deduce that a cluster-level contrast, aij=ci for all j, has Var(S)=σ2∑ici2ni{1+ρ(ni−1)}: inflated by the design effect.

  3. Deduce that a within-cluster contrast, ∑jaij=0 for every i, has Var(S)=σ2(1−ρ)∑ijaij2: deflated, by the factor 1−ρ<1.

  4. Show that the Pearson dispersion ϕ^P converges to 1 here, so it registers no overdispersion at all, and that no single ϕ can correct both kinds of contrast even if one were supplied by hand. Which device in the table is then the right one?

exr-ql-phi-cancels.title: A2
exr-ql-phi-cancels.html: Verify from @eq-ql-robust that the empirical sandwich does not change if V is replaced by cV for a constant c>0, and explain why this is to be expected.

exr-ql-power-cv.title: B2
exr-ql-power-cv.html: Under the power specification Var(Y)=ϕμξ, find the coefficient of variation Var(Y)/E(Y) as a function of μ. For which ξ is it constant? Which of the specifications in the table of this section have the property that a multiplicative change of units, Y↦cY, leaves the specification in the same family with a new ϕ?

exr-ql-quasi-table.title: A1
exr-ql-quasi-table.html: Compute ϕw−1Q(μ;y) from @eq-ql-quasi for V(μ)=1, V(μ)=μ, V(μ)=μ(1−μ) and V(μ)=μ2, and check that in each case it is the log-likelihood kernel of the corresponding family, up to a function of y alone.

exr-ql-size-in-q.title: A1
exr-ql-size-in-q.html: Show that for fixed ϕ0>1 the size @eq-ql-size tends to 1 as q→∞. (Use χ2(q)/q→1 in probability, together with χ1−α2(q)/q→1, and compare with the event χ2(q)/q>χ1−α2(q)/(qϕ0).)

exr-ql-when-equal.title: A1
exr-ql-when-equal.html: Under a log link and V(μ)=μ with wi≡1, suppose the true variances are σi2=τμi for an unknown τ>0. Show that the sandwich and the model-based covariance have the same probability limit, and identify what ϕ^P estimates. Repeat for σi2=τμi2 and show that the two then differ unless all μi are equal.

exr-ql-which-phi.title: A1
exr-ql-which-phi.html: For each of the following, say whether a dispersion parameter ϕ≠1 is meaningful, and why: (a) counts of insurance claims per policy; (b) the proportion of a litter of 12 pups showing a defect; (c) an indicator of whether a patient survived; (d) the proportion of 500 sampled voters supporting a candidate, the voters sampled in clusters of 10 households.

lem-ql-exchangeable.title: Exchangeable trials
lem-ql-exchangeable.html:
Let Z1,…,Zm be binary variables with common mean π and Cov(Zs,Zt)=ρπ(1−π) for all s≠t, so that ρ is their common correlation, and let Z¯=m−1∑tZt. Then E(Z¯)=π,Var(Z¯)={1+ρ(m−1)}π(1−π)m,{#eq-ql-exchangeable}

and ρ≥−1/(m−1), with ρ≥0 whenever the trials are conditionally independent and identically distributed given some unobserved variable.

prp-ql-dispersion.title: Estimating the dispersion, and quasi-deviance tests
prp-ql-dispersion.title_html: Estimating the dispersion, and quasi-deviance tests
prp-ql-dispersion.html:
Assume @eq-ql-specification with the mean model correct.

  1. E[wi(Yi−μi0)2/V(μi0)]=ϕ for every i, so the Pearson estimator ϕ^P=X2/(n−p) with X2=∑iwi(yi−μ^i)2/V(μ^i) — the statistic @eq-glm-pearson — is consistent for ϕ under (Q1)–(Q5). The divisor n−p is an analogy with s2 (@thm-lm-sigma2), exact only in the normal linear model.

  2. The deviance estimator 𝛍ϕ^D=D(y,μ^)/(n−p), with D the quasi-deviance @eq-ql-quasi-deviance, is not in general consistent for ϕ. The two agree only so far as a third-order remainder is negligible: large binomial groups and large Poisson means, not small counts. Only ϕ^P has expectation exactly ϕ at the true mean.

  3. For nested mean models C(X0)⊆C(X) with rank(X)−rank(X0)=q, fitted with the same V, the quasi-F statistic is 𝛍𝛍F={D(y,μ~)−D(y,μ^)}/qϕ^P.{#eq-ql-quasi-f}

    Under the reduced model and (Q1)–(Q5), qF→χ2(q), so referring F to F(q,n−p) is asymptotically correct and is the usual small-sample convention. If the variance specification is wrong the limit fails and the Wald statistic built from @eq-ql-robust should be used instead.

  4. No convention makes 𝛃−2Q(β^) a log-likelihood, so @def-sel-aic-bic does not apply. The criterion 𝛍QAIC=D(y,μ^)/ϕ^+2p, with ϕ^ fixed at its value in the largest model, is in common use, but it is a convention, not a theorem. Cross-validation (@def-sel-cv) needs no likelihood, and the analogue for correlated responses, the QIC of Chapter 40, rests on the same convention.

prp-ql-optimality.title: Godambe optimality
prp-ql-optimality.html:
Assume @eq-ql-specification, and consider linear estimating functions 𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛃𝛍g(β)=∑i=1nai(β){yi−μi(β)}=C(β)(y−μ), where C=[a1,…,an] is p×n, differentiable in 𝛃β, and does not depend on y. Let 𝛃S=−E{∂g/∂β⊤} and suppose S is nonsingular. Define the Godambe information 𝛃J(g)=S⊤Cov{g(β0)}−1S.

  1. Every such g is unbiased, and S=CDX.

  2. J(g)⪯ϕ−1X⊤WX=J(U) in the order of nonnegative definiteness, for every linear estimating function g.

  3. Equality holds if and only if C⊤=Σ−1DXN for a nonsingular p×p matrix N, with Σ=Cov(Y): the coefficients are those of the quasi-score up to one common nonsingular transformation, and g then has the same roots as U.

prp-ql-overdispersion.title: Sources of overdispersion, and the price of ignoring it
prp-ql-overdispersion.title_html: Sources of overdispersion, and the price of ignoring it
prp-ql-overdispersion.html:
1. Unobserved heterogeneity. Let Y∣Λ have mean Λ and variance V∗(Λ), and let Λ have mean μ and variance τ2, with 0<τ2<∞ and E{V∗(Λ)}<∞. Then EY=μ and VarY=E{V∗(Λ)}+τ2, which for a Poisson kernel V∗(λ)=λ is μ+τ2>μ: any unmodelled variation in the mean overdisperses.

  2. Clustering. If the response is an average of m units with pairwise correlation ρ>0, its variance is inflated by 1+ρ(m−1), by @lem-ql-exchangeable; the same factor applies to a sum of m correlated indicators.

  3. Contagion. Let Y=∑j=1NSj, where N is Poisson with mean ν and the Sj are independent copies of a positive integer-valued S with ES2<∞, independent of N: events arrive in clusters. Then EY=νES and VarY=νES2, so VarYEY=ES2ES ≥ ES ≥ 1,{#eq-ql-contagion}

    with equality throughout if and only if S≡1, that is unless the events arrive singly.

  4. Neither of the above. A wrong mean model, an omitted interaction or a few gross outliers all inflate X2, and no dispersion parameter repairs them; for ungrouped binary data a large X2 is always a statement about the mean model.

  5. The price. Suppose the mean model is correct and the true variances are σi2=ϕ0V(μi0)/wi with ϕ0≥1 unknown, while inference uses ϕ=1. Then under (Q1)–(Q5) any statistic of @prp-glm-three-tests for a q-dimensional hypothesis converges to ϕ0χ2(q), so a nominal level-α test has asymptotic size Pr{χ2(q)>χ1−α2(q)/ϕ0} ≥ α,{#eq-ql-size}

    increasing in ϕ0, and tending to 1 as q→∞ for every fixed ϕ0>1. Standard errors are too small by the factor ϕ01/2.

prp-ql-properties.title: What the quasi-likelihood does and does not share with a log-likelihood
prp-ql-properties.title_html: What the quasi-likelihood does and does not share with a log-likelihood
prp-ql-properties.html:
Write Q′=∂Q/∂μ. Then, for every variance specification:

  1. Q′(μ;y)=w(y−μ)/{ϕV(μ)}, and Q(μ;y)≤0 with equality only at μ=y: the quasi-likelihood is maximized at the observation, as a saturated fit would be;

  2. E{Q′(μ;Y)}=0 and Var{Q′(μ;Y)}=−E{∂2Q/∂μ2}=w/{ϕV(μ)}, the two Bartlett identities;

  3. if (V,ϕ,w) are those of an exponential dispersion family (@def-glm-edf), then Q(μ;y)=ℓ(μ;y)−ℓ(y;y), so Q is the log-likelihood measured from its saturated value, and 𝛃𝛍−2ϕQ(β)=D(y,μ) is the deviance of @eq-glm-deviance.

thm-ql-asymptotics.title: Consistency, normality and the sandwich
thm-ql-asymptotics.html:
Assume (Q1)–(Q5). Then:

  1. 𝛃𝛃Bn−1/2An(β^−β0) →d Np(0,I),{#eq-ql-sandwich-limit}

    so that 𝛃β^ behaves as if its covariance were the sandwich An−1BnAn−1, which involves the distribution of Y only through its first two moments.

  2. If the variance specification @eq-ql-specification is correct, then Bn=An by @thm-ql-score(d), and @eq-ql-sandwich-limit becomes 𝛃𝛃An1/2(β^−β0)→Np(0,I): the model-based covariance An−1=ϕ(X⊤WX)−1 is correct, and by @prp-ql-optimality no linear estimating function has a larger Godambe information — hence, whenever (Q1)–(Q5) hold for that estimating function too, none has a smaller asymptotic covariance.

  3. Let c^i=wih′(η^i)/V(μ^i) and define the empirical sandwich Σ^rob=(X⊤W^X)−1{∑i=1nc^i2(yi−μ^i)2x(i)x(i)⊤}(X⊤W^X)−1,{#eq-ql-robust}

    in which ϕ cancels. Then nΣ^rob−nAn−1BnAn−1→0 in probability, and @eq-ql-sandwich-limit holds with 𝛃𝛃Σ^rob−1/2(β^−β0) in place of the left-hand side.

thm-ql-score.title: The quasi-score
thm-ql-score.html:
Let 𝛃𝛃U(β)=∂Q/∂β be the quasi-score, and keep the notation W=diag{wih′(ηi)2/V(μi)} and D=diag{h′(ηi)} of @thm-glm-score. Write An=ϕ−1X⊤WX. Then:

  1. 𝛃𝛍U(β)=ϕ−1X⊤WD−1(y−μ), which is @eq-glm-score exactly. The estimating equations 𝛃U(β^)=0 are @eq-ql-equations, they do not involve ϕ, and they are solved by the iteratively reweighted least squares of @thm-glm-irls;

  2. if the mean model is correct then 𝛃EU(β0)=0, whatever the true variances are: the quasi-score is an unbiased estimating function;

  3. 𝛃−E{∂U/∂β⊤}=An, again whatever the true variances are;

  4. if in addition the variance specification @eq-ql-specification is correct, then 𝛃Cov{U(β0)}=An as well: sensitivity and variability agree, which is the second Bartlett identity for Q;

  5. if instead Var(Yi)=σi2 for arbitrary σi2, then 𝛃Cov{U(β0)}=Bn=1ϕ2∑i=1n{wih′(ηi)V(μi)}2σi2x(i)x(i)⊤,{#eq-ql-meat}

    which equals An if and only if ∑i{wihi′/Vi}2{σi2−ϕVi/wi}x(i)x(i)⊤=0.
